71346-the-young-ship-builder.title: The Young Ship Builder
71346-the-young-ship-builder.creator: Unknown
71346-the-young-ship-builder.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. They named me after my Grandmother Dill, because she was a woman who feared the Lord. It was my father’s behest, and was so set down in his will--he died just after I was born. The will was pasted into the family Bible. Every one said it was a beautiful will, because, while he had scarcely any material possessions, he yet bequeathed so much.

arxiv-1810-08579.title: Learning to Recognize Discontiguous Entities
arxiv-1810-08579.creator: Aldrian Obaja Muis, Wei Lu
arxiv-1810-08579.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Aldrian Obaja Muis, Wei Lu. This paper focuses on the study of recognizing discontiguous entities. Motivated by a previous work, we propose to use a novel hypergraph representation to jointly encode discontiguous entities of unbounded length, which can overlap with one another.

arxiv-2012-12658.title: Entanglement Devised Barren Plateau Mitigation
arxiv-2012-12658.creator: Taylor L. Patti, Khadijeh Najafi, Xun Gao, Susanne F. Yelin
arxiv-2012-12658.description: Abstract Hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithms are one of the most propitious implementations of quantum computing on near-term devices, offering classical machine learning support to quantum scale solution spaces. However, numerous studies have demonstrated that the rate at which this space grows in qubit number could preclude learning in deep quantum circuits, a phenomenon known as barren plateaus.

arxiv-2104-13446.title: Semi-On-Policy Training for Sample Efficient Multi-Agent Policy Gradients Conference: Proc. of the 20th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2021); May 3–7, 2021; London, UK ???
arxiv-2104-13446.creator: Bozhidar Vasilev, Tarun Gupta, Bei Peng, Shimon Whiteson
arxiv-2104-13446.description: Abstract . Policy gradient methods are an attractive approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning problems due to their convergence properties and robustness in partially observable scenarios. However, there is a significant performance gap between state-of-the-art policy gradient and value-based methods on the popular StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC) benchmark.

arxiv-2106-05083.creator: Damianos Iosifidis ∗ , Nurgissa Myrzakulov †,⋆ , Ratbay Myrzakulov †,⋆
arxiv-2106-05083.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Damianos Iosifidis ∗ , Nurgissa Myrzakulov †,⋆ , Ratbay Myrzakulov †,⋆. We derive the full set of field equations for the Metric-Affine version of the Myrzakulov gravity model and also extend this family of theories to a broader one.

arxiv-2301-10134.title: Bipartite Graph Diffusion Model for Human Interaction Generation
arxiv-2301-10134.creator: Baptiste Chopin, Hao Tang, Mohamed Daoudi, Inria, Université Côte d’Azur, France, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA, Univ. Lille, CNRS, Centrale Lille, Institut Mines-Télécom, UMR 9189 CRIStAL, Lille, F-59000, France, IMT Nord Europe, Institut Mines-Télécom, Univ. Lille, Centre for Digital
arxiv-2301-10134.description: Abstract The generation of natural human motion interactions is a hot topic in computer vision and computer animation. It is a challenging task due to the diversity of possible human motion interactions. Diffusion models, which have already shown remarkable generative capabilities in other domains, are a good candidate for this task.

arxiv-2302-07555.title: Firmware implementation of a recurrent neural network for the computation of the energy deposited in the liquid argon calorimeter of the ATLAS experiment
arxiv-2302-07555.creator: N. Sur
arxiv-2302-07555.description: Abstract The ATLAS experiment measures the properties of particles that are products of proton-proton collisions at the LHC. The ATLAS detector will undergo a major upgrade before the high luminosity phase of the LHC. The ATLAS liquid argon calorimeter measures the energy of particles interacting electromagnetically in the detector.

arxiv-2303-10688.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing on an optical transition via emergent collective quantum correlations
arxiv-2303-10688.creator: Johannes Franke, Sean R. Muleady, Raphael Kaubruegger, Florian Kranzl, Rainer Blatt, Ana Maria Rey, Manoj K. Joshi, Christian F. Roos
arxiv-2303-10688.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Johannes Franke, Sean R. Muleady, Raphael Kaubruegger, Florian Kranzl, Rainer Blatt, Ana Maria Rey, Manoj K. Joshi, Christian F. Roos. The control over quantum states in atomic systems has led to the most precise optical atomic clocks to date Bothwell et al. Their sensitivity is currently bounded by the standard quantum limit, a fundamental floor set by quantum mechanics for uncorrelated particles, which can nevertheless be overcome when operated with entangled particles.

arxiv-2312-11883.title: EMU/GAMA: Radio detected galaxies are more obscured than optically selected galaxies DOI: 10.1017/pasa.2020.32
arxiv-2312-11883.creator: U. T. Ahmed, A. M. Hopkins, J. Ware, Y. A. Gordon, M. Bilicki, M. J. I. Brown, M. Cluver, G. Gürkan, Á. R. López-Sánchez, D. A. Leahy, L. Marchetti, S. Phillipps, I. Prandoni, N. Seymour, E. N. Taylor, E. Vardoulaki
arxiv-2312-11883.description: Abstract We demonstrate the importance of radio selection in probing heavily obscured galaxy populations. We combine Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) Early Science data in the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) G23 field with the GAMA data, providing optical photometry and spectral line measurements, together with Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) infrared (IR) photometry, providing IR luminosities and colours.

arxiv-2401-09030.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean Field Games with Common Noise Thanks: De-xuan Xu, Zhun Gou, and Nan-jing Huang: The work of these authors was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (12171339).
arxiv-2401-09030.creator: De-xuan Xu, Zhun Gou, Nan-jing Huang and Shuang Gao a. Department of Mathematics, Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan 610064, P.R. Chinab. College of Mathematics and Statistics, Chongqing Technology and Business University, Chongqing 400067, P.R. Chinac. Department of Electrical Engineering, Polyte
arxiv-2401-09030.description: Abstract Abstract. This paper studies linear quadratic graphon mean field games (LQ-GMFGs) with common noise, in which a large number of agents are coupled via a weighted undirected graph. One special feature, compared with the well-studied graphon mean field games, is that the states of agents are described by the dynamic systems with the idiosyncratic noises and common noise.

arxiv-2505-03396.title: On the quantitative lower bounds for solutions to the Boltzmann equation in nonconvex domains
arxiv-2505-03396.creator: Jhe-kuan SU
arxiv-2505-03396.description: Abstract . In this article, we study the continuous mild solutions to the Boltzmann equation in a bounded spatial domain, under either angular cutoff assumption or non-cutoff assumption. Without assuming convexity of the spatial domain, we establish a Maxwellian lower bound in the cutoff case, and a weaker-than-Maxwellian lower bound for the non-cutoff case.

arxiv-2602-02427.title: Embedding Perturbation may Better Reflect the Uncertainty in LLM Reasoning
arxiv-2602-02427.creator: Qihao Wen, Jiahao Wang, Yang Nan, Pengfei He, Ravi Tandon, Han Xu
arxiv-2602-02427.description: Abstract Large language Models (LLMs) have achieved significant breakthroughs across diverse domains; however, they can still produce unreliable or misleading outputs. For responsible LLM application, Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques are used to estimate a model’s uncertainty about its outputs, indicating the likelihood that those outputs may be problematic.

europmc-pmc11299546.creator: Gaser C, Dahnke R, Thompson PM, Kurth F, Luders E, The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.

Here we introduce the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT)-a powerful suite of tools for brain morphometric analyses...

pmc-10480465.title: Long-lived spin waves in a metallic antiferromagnet
pmc-10480465.creator: G. Poelchen, J. Hellwig, M. Peters, D. Yu. Usachov, K. Kliemt, C. Laubschat, P. M. Echenique, E. V. Chulkov, C. Krellner, S. S. P. Parkin, D. V. Vyalikh, A. Ernst, K. Kummer
pmc-10480465.description: Collective spin excitations in magnetically ordered crystals, called magnons or spin waves, can serve as carriers in novel spintronic devices with ultralow energy consumption. The generation of well-detectable spin flows requires long lifetimes of high-frequency magnons. In general, the lifetime of spin waves in a metal is substantially reduced due to a strong coupling of magnons to the Stoner continuum.

pmc-11436595.title: Aeromonas veronii-associated bacteremia in the course of treatment of acute myeloid leukemia: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-11436595.creator: Jiashan Zhao, Tianjiao Wu, Songyun Wang, Huirui Wang
pmc-11436595.description: PurposeThis study aimed to report a case of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) complicated by Aeromonas veronii infection-induced bacteremia and to review relevant literature on the etiology, prevention, treatment, and prognosis of bacteremia in immunocompromised populations, aiming to reduce mortality in individuals with hematologic and other end-stage diseases and improve patient outcomes.

pmc-11481478.title: Central retinal artery occlusion as the initial manifestation of mixed connective tissue disease in a young woman: a case report
pmc-11481478.creator: Kou Liu, Yuzhu Liu, Xiaohan Yang, Li Cui, Chunli Chen
pmc-11481478.description: BackgroundRetinal artery occlusions are rare amongst young adults, and relevant risk factors and etiology remain unclear. In this report, we present a case of central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) as the initial manifestation of mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) in a young woman.

pmc-12421516.title: Prevalence and factors associated with HIV viral rebound in individuals on ART: A systematic review study
pmc-12421516.creator: Lindokuhle Ndlazi, Mathildah M. Mokgatle, Lindiwe P. Cele, Raikane J. Seretlo
pmc-12421516.description: BackgroundViral rebound (VR), the resurgence of detectable human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) viral loads (> 50 copies/mL) after suppression, remains a challenge for individuals on antiretroviral therapy (ART) in South Africa, despite free access to treatment.AimThis systematic review aimed to determine the prevalence of HIV VR and its contributing factors among individuals on ART.

pmc-12565977.title: Scapular Dyskinesis and Associated Factors in Adult Elite Swimmers
pmc-12565977.creator: Se Young Joo, Young Kyun Kim, Ramona Ritzmann, Luis Suárez-Arrones, Francisco Javier Núñez Sánchez
pmc-12565977.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: Swimmers are repeatedly exposed to overhead shoulder movements, which overload the surrounding soft tissue and may contribute to shoulder pain. These repetitive demands have also been implicated in the development of scapular dyskinesis (SD). This cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of SD and to examine its associations with extrinsic and intrinsic factors in adult elite swimmers. Materials and Methods: Fifty competitive swimmers (mean age, 23.9 years; mean training experience, 13.6 years) participated in this study.

pmc-12587223.title: Discrepancies between current displayed and auto‐logged glucose values in FreeStyle Libre 3: Implications for clinical interpretation
pmc-12587223.creator: Lilian Witthauer, Camilo Mendez, José Garcia‐Tirado, Manuel Eichenlaub, Delia Waldenmaier, Stefan Pleus, Guido Freckmann
pmc-12587223.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). AimsThe FreeStyle Libre 3 (FSL3) continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system provides both auto‐logged glucose values (AL) and current displayed glucose values (CUR). These values are often assumed to be interchangeable; however, discrepancies and their clinical relevance remain underexplored.Materials and methodsData from a 15‐day study in 24 study participants wearing FSL3 were analysed, including three in‐clinic sessions with glycaemic excursions during which CUR values were retrieved every 15 min by study personnel.

pmc-13054892.title: Quantum coherence enhancement through control of metal–ligand covalency: modulating spin–orbit coupling in isostructural molecular qubits
pmc-13054892.creator: Subrata Ghosh, Paul H. Oyala, Maksym Fizer, Vsevolod D. Dergachev, Sergey A. Varganov, Natia L. Frank
pmc-13054892.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Manipulation of quantum systems for sensing and transduction rely on controlling the interactions between a quantum system and the many degrees of freedom of the bath. In molecular spin quantum systems, spin–orbit coupling serves as a conduit for energy dissipation via vibrational and phonon modes, which in turn are dictated by changes in oxidation state, metal–ligand covalency, and symmetry of the coordination sphere.

pmc-13191272.title: Development of a photocatalytic membrane screening reactor (PMSR) for standardized evaluation of immobilized photocatalytic support materials
pmc-13191272.creator: Michael S. Leupold, Anam Asghar, Klaus Kerpen, Lukas Fischer, Torsten C. Schmidt
pmc-13191272.description: Reliable screening of photocatalytic materials for water purification requires laboratory-scale reactors with well-defined irradiation conditions and reproducible operation. Therefore, in this work, a compact, batch-mode photocatalytic membrane screening reactor (PMSR) designed for rapid, high-throughput evaluation of photocatalytic performance under controlled conditions is presented.

pmc-13326539.title: Mycobacterium shinjukuense pulmonary disease in a young woman: a case report and literature review
pmc-13326539.creator: Siwei Gu, Chunlei Wang, Binghuai Lu, Xiaojing Cui
pmc-13326539.description: BackgroundMycobacterium shinjukuense is a rare type of non-tuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) first reported in Japan. Reported cases of Mycobacterium shinjukuense pulmonary diseases are rare where hosts exhibited apparent risk factors for NTM infection. No consensus has been made on its treatment regimen.

pmc-13565129.title: Patient experiences and decision-making priorities in early esophageal cancer: a qualitative interview study
pmc-13565129.creator: Kirsty Cole, Pradeep Bhandari, Michael White, Tim Underwood, Sheraz Markar, Philip Pucher, the Association of Upper GI Surgery GB&I (AUGIS)
pmc-13565129.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryEndoscopic resection (ER) may offer organ preserving treatment in early (cT1N0) esophago-gastric (OG) cancer. Resectional surgery after ER may be recommended if pathological factors suggesting a risk of occult nodal metastasis are identified. Decision-making in this setting is complex, as patients must weigh the unknown risk of cancer progression with surveillance, against the more tangible and measurable impact of major surgery. Understanding patient priorities and values in making this decision is essential to support informed, patient-centered care.
